deities: Chhotti Bambleshwari shrine at the hill base, about 0.5 km from the main complex
festivals: Navaratri — Sharad (Dussehra) and Chaitra (Ram Navami), with Jyoti Kalash

history.dynasty: Legend: King Veersen (~2200 years ago); Kalachuri King Karnadeva credited with an 11th-century renovation (single source); present structure rebuilt early 20th century by Rani Rupmati of Dongargarh (per sacredsites)
history.period: Ancient site; present marble-tiled structure early 20th century (recent renovations ongoing)
history.summary: The Bambleshwari Temple is the hilltop shrine of Dongargarh, set 1,600 ft up and reached by about 1,100 steps (or by ropeway — the only passenger ropeway in Chhattisgarh). Legend says that around 2,200 years ago the childless King Veersen performed puja on his priests' advice and was blessed with a son, Madansen, after which he built the temple to Shiva and Parvati's grace; after the deaths of the lovers Maadhavnal and Kaamkandla, a guilt-stricken King Vikramaditya's worship brought forth Maa Bagulamukhi, who agreed to reside here — and the name is said to have shifted from Bagulamukhi to Bamlai to Bamleshwari. This main shrine is the Badi Bambleshwari; a Chhotti Bambleshwari stands at ground level about half a kilometre away. CONFLICTS: the legend's age is given as 2,200 years in most sources but 2,500 in one; the 11th-century Kalachuri renovation and the Rani Rupmati rebuilding are reported by sacredsites alone and are not corroborated elsewhere. A 2016 ropeway accident killed several people (per Wikipedia's Dongargarh article) — confirm current ropeway status locally. CSV CORRECTION: town 'Rajnandgaon' is the district headquarters ~40 km away; the temple is at Dongargarh — corrected. Coordinates are Wikipedia/GeoHack for the hilltop temple.

name: Maa Bambleshwari Temple
town_description: Dongargarh is a municipal town in Rajnandgaon district, about 40 km west of Rajnandgaon, its name joining 'dongar' (mountain) and 'garh' (fort). It is dominated by the 1,600-ft hill carrying the Bambleshwari temple and is one of Chhattisgarh's major pilgrimage towns.

travel.railway: Dongargarh station on the Mumbai-Howrah main line; the temple is visible from the station, about a 15-minute walk to the hill base.
travel.road: About 40 km from Rajnandgaon; a ropeway runs up the hill (confirm current operation locally).

visitor_information.best_time: October to March for pleasant weather; both Navaratris draw lakhs of pilgrims.
visitor_information.opening_hours: One source reports 4 AM-12 PM on weekdays and 5 AM-10 PM on holidays, but this is uncorroborated — verify locally before travel.
